objective: Recover a trustworthy model of an unfamiliar or messy repository, then make one evidence-backed improvement without broad speculative cleanup or automatic cross-repository expansion.

stages.purpose: Preserve current state, anchor the active repository/work target, and establish the smallest trustworthy discovery surface: governing instructions, declared current/canonical entrypoints, relevant dependency/coordination records, manifests, relevant modules/tests/CI, recent history, and material source authority/freshness.
stages.exit_when: The active work target, current technical surface, authoritative entrypoints, and material source/dependency authority needed for the immediate recovery decision are known without recursively traversing unrelated reference or repository graphs.

stages.purpose: Separate intended product behavior from accidental/stale implementation, reconcile current/draft/historical/unknown and external-repository evidence without erasing conflicts, and identify the highest-leverage blocker.
evidence: README/spec versus code comparison when material
tests versus runtime behavior when material
external repository source/revision/status when a material claim is owned there
explicit unresolved conflicts when no justified winner exists
stages.exit_when: A concise current-state model and prioritized recovery target are defensible from evidence, with repository boundaries, conflicts, and uncertainty preserved rather than silently expanded or resolved.

stages.purpose: Fix or stabilize one high-value path in the active work target before broad refactoring, using the reconstructed current baseline rather than stale artifacts or external repositories as accidental implementation authority.
evidence: evidence that the chosen path follows the current source of truth
explicit separate authorization if another repository also requires mutation
stages.exit_when: One meaningful path is more trustworthy and the next recovery priority is clearer without unrequested cross-repository mutation.

pressure_guards.rule: Do not equate newest file, merged branch, or most detailed document with current truth. Track material source role/authority and freshness; Draft/Proposed/Historical evidence remains non-authoritative unless the project explicitly says otherwise.
When material sources disagree and authority/freshness do not justify a winner, preserve the conflict and uncertainty instead of silently selecting or rewriting history.

Start from explicit project first-read/current/canonical entrypoints when available. Treat links, related/depends_on metadata, registries, indexes, historical release lists, directory inventories, and repository maps as navigation rather than mandatory coverage. Follow an edge only when it can change the immediate route, baseline, target, acceptance evidence, dependency status, or risk boundary; stop once the recovery target is defensible.

A referenced upstream/downstream repository is evidence or dependency scope, not automatically an active work target. Cross repositories only when a material claim is owned there or a local dependency/coordination record is stale, ambiguous, or insufficient; read the smallest authoritative source/revision needed, then return to the active repository. Evidence access does not authorize mutation, and product evidence must not be silently promoted into shared protocol/governance by cross-repository edits.

escalations.when: The project needs durable reconstruction of intent/specifications before continued feature work.
escalations.selection_rule: Prefer core Spec Kit existing-project/evolving-spec workflows first; treat community brownfield extensions as untrusted candidates until source and permissions are reviewed.

escalations.when: The repository is too large or long-running for the current host to maintain reliable context and isolated subproblems after bounded discovery has already identified the relevant surface.
escalations.selection_rule: Select the runtime property actually missing; do not migrate merely because the repository is messy, cross-referenced, or exposes a large reference graph.

escalations.when: Recovery reveals that the immediate blocker is a bounded reproducible defect.
escalations.selection_rule: Reroute to bug-fix first; use mini-SWE-agent only if the issue is clear and verifiable.

verification: current-state claims are grounded in repository/runtime evidence
material sources have authority/freshness considered rather than being flattened into one truth
reference/repository graphs were traversed only for material unresolved questions
external repository reads were justified by claim ownership or stale/insufficient local dependency evidence
cross-repository writes did not occur without separate scope/authorization
broad cleanup or exhaustive repository reading was avoided unless evidence justified it
reroute_signals: a specific failing behavior becomes primary -> bug-fix
a desired new behavior becomes primary -> feature-change
the user only needs a decision/review -> understand-review
